The words

'Tis midnight, and on Olive's brow
The star is dimmed that lately shone;
'Tis midnight, in the garden now
The suff'ring Savior prays alone.

'Tis midnight, and from all removed
Immanuel wrestles, lone, with fears;
E'en the disciple whom He loved
Heeds not his Master's grief and tears.

'Tis midnight, from the heav'nly plains
Are borne the songs that angels know;
Unheard by mortals are the strains
That sweetly soothe the Savior's woe.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum F and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on d (F).
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

The words are by William Bingham Tappan, first published in 1822. The tune, ST. CROSS, is by John Bacchus Dykes (1861). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.

  • Words (1822): William Bingham Tappan (1794–1849)
  • Music (1861): John Bacchus Dykes (1823–1876)

Questions about 'Tis Midnight and on Olive's Brow

What is the doh of 'Tis Midnight and on Olive's Brow?

In this version, in D minor, doh is F. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does 'Tis Midnight and on Olive's Brow start on?

It starts on d (F in D minor). Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

Is 'Tis Midnight and on Olive's Brow in the public domain?

Yes. William Bingham Tappan died in 1849, John Bacchus Dykes died in 1876; the words were first published in 1822 and the music in 1861. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
